subject: Post-call: Performance targets & throughput commitments (FinTechCo)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Vargas <sofia.v@fintechco.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Performance targets & throughput commitments (FinTechCo)

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned on sizing for the pilot and the technical deep-dive: 

TL;DR (numbers you confirmed on the call)
- Steady-state average QPS: 12 requests/sec (write workloads that hit the API)
- Typical request size: ~300 tokens/request (avg prompt + completion)
- Steady-state tokens/sec: ~3,600 tokens/sec (12 QPS * 300 tokens)
- Peak event day pattern: 18:00 daily release window produces spikes of ~220 QPS sustained for ~90s (burst windows), with per-request tokens similar (~300) — peak tokens/sec ~66,000 during release bursts.
- Concurrency expectation (simultaneous active requests): steady ~40, peak ~700 during the release window.
- Latency SLO: p95 & p99 targets are 150ms / 300ms for non-streaming generation; streaming minimum frame latency target is 80ms for first byte.

What we’ll do next (Mutual action plan)
1) Redwood: run an initial sizing doc + quick bench using your uploaded sample traces (attached fintechco_throughput_snapshot.csv). Deliverable: recommended pool type (dedicated vs. hosted burst), estimated GPU-count, and expected cost delta. ETA: 2 business days.
2) FinTechCo: confirm daily release cadence and attachment of the .xlsx (MAU and QPS estimates) we discussed, and share any recent 7-day request distribution histograms.
3) Schedule technical deep-dive with CloudOps (Marco) to validate network egress patterns and tokenization anomalies — suggest a 60-min slot next week.

A few clarifications from the call I captured:
- The streaming use-case (live user chat) is ~10% of overall traffic but drives latency sensitivity; it’s a few hundred simultaneous websockets at peak.
- Some requests include multi-turn context up to ~1,200 tokens occasionally; we should include an upper-bound sequencing test.

Attachments referenced: fintechco_throughput_snapshot.csv (sample day traces), mau_and_qps_estimates.xlsx (sales-provided projections).

If those numbers look off to you, call it out and we’ll adjust the sizing. Otherwise I’ll start the bench and circulate Redwood’s sizing doc.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Vargas <sofia.v@fintechco.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Silva <msilva@cloudops.fintechco.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance targets & throughput commitments (FinTechCo)

Thanks, Dylan — useful recap. A few small corrections and extra details from our ops side: 

Corrections / clarifications:
- Steady-state QPS: 12 is correct for API-facing write ops, but remember reads (ruler queries) are separate and add ~3 QPS average. For this evaluation please focus on the write path only.
- Peak burst we said can reach short spikes of ~280 QPS for ~60–120s (we see this on release days). The 220 number is conservative; plan for 280 for sizing.
- Average tokens/request: after sampling 500 requests this morning, the mean landed closer to 260 tokens; heavy multi-turn cases (5% of requests) can be 1,200–1,500 tokens.
- Concurrency: our app queues at the edge so active backend concurrency is usually lower; your 700 peak is reasonable as an upper bound.

Additional data attached: mau_and_qps_estimates.xlsx (includes hourly cadence for peak day + MAU buckets). Marco will send the 7-day histograms separately.

One ask on SLA: for the pilot we need Redwood to demonstrate p95 <= 200ms on a 30-minute sustained load at 50 QPS with our median token mix. Can you confirm Redwood can run that test as part of the sizing run?

Also: procurement looped me in — I’ll add procurement@fintechco.com once we finalize the pilot scope and term.

Best,
Sofia
Head of Product, FinTechCo
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Performance targets & throughput commitments (FinTechCo)

Team — forwarding FinTechCo confirmations and attachments. Key asks and internal action items below.

Action items for Redwood (owner/time):
- Jordan: run a 30-minute sustained load test at 50 QPS with median token mix (260 tokens/request) and produce p95/p99 figures and CPU/GPU utilization traces. Target: demonstrate p95 <= 200ms as requested by customer. ETA: Tues 11/24 EOD.
- Ava: prepare two capacity recommendations: (A) hosted multi-tenant with burst credits for pilot, and (B) small Dedicated pool (specify GPUs and expected throughput). Include cost estimates and fallback policy for release spikes (auto-burst vs. queueing). ETA: Wed 11/25 midday.
- Dylan: run a quick high-burst bench to reproduce a 280 QPS ~90s spike using the attached sample trace and collect tokens/sec, memory, and observed latency. Share raw bench logs and a short synopsis in INF-927. ETA: Mon 11/23.

Notes: include an upper-bound test for 1,500-token requests at low QPS to validate KV cache and memory behavior. Jordan/Ava, flag any infra blockers.

Attachments from FinTechCo are saved to the deal folder: fintechco_throughput_snapshot.csv, mau_and_qps_estimates.xlsx. Link to our internal ticket: https://redwood-inference.atlassian.net/browse/INF-927

—Dylan
